name: Dumbbell Pullover
summary: An arcing movement where a single dumbbell travels from over the chest to behind the head. It stretches and trains the lats and chest, and works from the floor or a sofa edge.
setup: Lie on your back on the floor or across a bench, with knees bent and feet flat.
Hold one end of a dumbbell with both hands, palms facing up under the top plate.
Press it over your chest with a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Keeping your elbows slightly bent and fixed, lower the dumbbell in an arc back behind your head.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your lats and chest, or when your arms are about level with your ears.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest using your lats, moving along the same arc.
Keep your ribs down so the lower back does not arch.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the bottom: reduce the range and keep ribs down.
Bending and straightening the elbows like a triceps extension: keep the elbow angle constant.
Using too heavy a weight: choose a load you can control with both hands and no strain on the shoulders.
Letting the dumbbell slip: grip the inside of the top plate firmly with both palms.
